issues.failure_explanation: The map $\psi\mapsto\wh\psi$ is non-injective, so $\wh{\Aa}\wh\psi:=\wh{\Aa\psi}$ is not a well-defined operator on $\wh{\Ff}_{NM}$: $\sum c_i\wh\psi_i=0$ does not imply $\sum c_i\psi_i=0$, so $\sum c_i\wh{\Aa\psi_i}$ need not vanish. The proof's key step $\sum_i c_i\langle\wh{\Aa}\wh\psi_i,\wh\psi_j\rangle=\langle\wh{\Aa}\sum c_i\wh\psi_i,\wh\psi_j\rangle=0$ uses exactly this. Counterexample: $M=1,N=2$, $\psi_1(x_1)=\psi_2(x_1)=1$, $\Aa\psi_1(x_1)=1$, $\Aa\psi_2(x_1)=0$; then $\wh{\bm A}_{NM}=\begin{pmatrix}1/2&0\\1/2&0\end{pmatrix}$ and the prescribed formula sends the zero vector $\wh\psi_1-\wh\psi_2$ to $(\wh\psi_1+\wh\psi_2)/2\neq0$, so $\wh{\Aa}_{NM}$ is not an operator on $\wh{\Ff}_{NM}$ and 'the projection of $\wh{\Aa}$' is meaningless. The theorem holds only when $\wh{\bm G}_{NM}$ is invertible, the very case the paper claims to go beyond.

failure_location.quote: Then the matrix $\wh{\bm{A}}_{NM}$ which approximates $\wh{\Aa}$ is, with probability $1$, a matrix representation of the projection of $\wh{\Aa}$ onto $\wh{\Ff}_{NM}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the theorem either for invertible $\wh{\bm G}_{NM}$, or reinterpret $\wh{\Aa}_{NM}$ as the well-defined map $\Ff_N\to\wh{\Ff}_{NM}$, $\sum c_i\psi_i\mapsto\sum_{i,k}c_i[\wh{\bm A}_{NM}]_{ki}\wh\psi_k$, and prove it equals $\Pp_{\wh{\Ff}_{NM}}\circ\wh{(\cdot)}\circ\Aa|_{\Ff_N}$ (which follows from $\wh{\bm C}=\wh{\bm A}^\top\wh{\bm G}$); adjust the corollary accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The central Section 3 claim that the pseudoinverse estimator is a projection without invertibility of the empirical Gram matrix is unsupported; the first part of Corollary exact approximation ($\wh{\Aa}_{NM}=\wh{\Aa_N}$ with probability 1) is likewise ill-defined. Results for $M\ge m_0$ (invertible case) are unaffected.
issues.title: Induced operator $\wh{\Aa}$ and $\wh{\Aa}_{NM}$ are not well defined on $\wh{\Ff}_{NM}$ when $\wh{\Psi}$ is linearly dependent
issues.why_classification: A comparable result survives by changing the domain of the operator, but the stated object (an endomorphism of $\wh{\Ff}_{NM}$) must be replaced and the corollary restated; this is a contained but nontrivial reformulation.

issues.failure_explanation: The hypothesis requires $\|\Pp_{\Ff_N}\phi-\phi\|_\Ff=O(N^{-\alpha})$ for every $\phi\in\Ff$. Read uniformly (constant depending only on $\|\phi\|$, as the corollary's constant claim and the proof of Theorem OC theorem require), this says $\|Id-\Pp_{\Ff_N}\|\le CN^{-\alpha}$, impossible since $\|Id-\Pp_{\Ff_N}\|=1$ whenever $\Ff$ is infinite-dimensional. Read pointwise, it is still impossible: for nested finite-dimensional $\Ff_N$ with dense union one can pick orthonormal $e_k\in\Ff_{N_k}\cap\Ff_{N_{k-1}}^\perp$ along a sparse subsequence and $\phi=\sum a_ke_k\in\Ff$ with $\|\phi-\Pp_{\Ff_{N_{k-1}}}\phi\|\ge|a_k|$ decaying slower than $N_{k-1}^{-\alpha}$. Hence the corollary and the second parts of Theorems OC theorem and OC theorem noise have empty hypotheses and establish no rate.

issues.failure_explanation: With $\bm g=\Psi_N(\bm x)+\bm\eta$, mean-zero noise independent of $\bm x$ gives $\E[\bm g\bm g^\dagger]=\bm G_N+\E[\bm\eta\bm\eta^\dagger]\neq\bm G_N$ (and similarly for $\bm T_N$, and for $\bm C_N$ unless $\E[\bm\xi\bm\eta^\dagger]=0$, which Assumption noise assumption does not impose). Hence $\bm S^{\bm G}_m$ in \eqref{sum def} is not centred and Bernstein's inequality does not apply; $\tl{\bm G}_{NM}\to\bm G_N+\mathrm{Cov}(\bm\eta)$. Counterexample: $N=1$, $\psi\equiv1$, $\Aa\psi\equiv1$, $\xi=0$, $\eta=\pm\sigma$ Rademacher: $\tl{\bm G}\to1+\sigma^2$, $\tl{\bm C}\to1$, so $\tl{\bm A}\to1/(1+\sigma^2)\neq \bm A_N=1$, and the claimed bound $\|\tl\Aa_{NM}-\Aa_N\|\le c\delta$ fails for small $\delta$ no matter how large $M$ is.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must restrict to noise only in $\Aa\psi$ evaluations ($\bm\eta=0$, with $\bm\xi$ independent of $\bm x$), or introduce a bias-corrected estimator (subtracting the noise covariance) and reprove the concentration bounds around the corrected target.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition noise bound, Theorem OC theorem noise, the noisy rate \eqref{order of convergence noise}, and the Gaussian-noise discussion in Example noise example 1 are invalid whenever the dictionary evaluations carry noise ($\bm\eta\neq0$); the abstract's claim to account for noisy observations is not supported in that regime.
issues.title: Noisy dictionary evaluations bias the Gram/structure matrices: $\E[\bm g\bm g^\dagger]\neq\bm G_N$
issues.why_classification: The estimator converges to the wrong limit in the advertised noisy-dictionary regime, so that regime must be excluded or a new estimator and argument built; the primary claim does not survive as stated.

issues.failure_explanation: $\tl{\PP}$ conditions on the event $E$ that all $M$ noise vectors are bounded, so $\PP(A)\ge\PP(A\cap E)=\PP(E)\tl{\PP}(A)$ with $\PP(E)=\tl p_N^M$ by independence, not $\tl p_N$. The proof only obtains $\tl{\PP}[\cdot]\ge p/\tl p_N$ and then wrongly infers $\PP[\cdot]\ge p$; the correct inference gives $\PP[\cdot]\ge\tl p_N^{M-1}p$, which tends to 0 as $M\to\infty$ when $\tl p_N<1$ (e.g. Gaussian noise). The stated sample-size condition therefore does not deliver probability $p$.

The first (unconditional) part of the theorem is therefore not established as stated.

issues.failure_explanation: Boundedness of each $\Aa_N$ does not imply a uniform bound on $(\lambda_N)$. From $\|f_N\|_\Dd=1$ one only gets $|\lambda_N|\le1/\|f_N\|_\Ff$, which is unbounded if $\|f_N\|_\Ff\to0$. Counterexample: $\Aa=d^2/dx^2$ on the torus with the Fourier dictionary; $\Aa_N$ has eigenpairs $\lambda_N=-N^2$, $f_N=e^{iNx}/\sqrt{1+N^4}$ with $\|f_N\|_\Dd=1$, so $(\lambda_N)$ has no convergent subsequence and the theorem's first assertion fails. The same unjustified assertion is made for $(\lambda_{NM})$ in Theorem convergence eigenfunctions joint theorem.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that the chosen eigenvalue sequence is bounded (or that $\Aa$ is bounded), and state the theorems as: any bounded sequence of eigenpairs has a subsequence converging to an eigenpair of $\Aa$ (when the weak limit is nonzero).

Additionally, the step $\langle(\Aa-\Aa_{N_i,M'})f_{N_i,M'},g\rangle\to0$ is justified only by pointwise convergence on fixed vectors, whereas $f_{N_i,M'}$ varies (it does follow from the uniform bound $1/(2N)$ in the proof of Theorem joint limit theorem and a weak-convergence argument, but this is not given).
